answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bonding curve on attested identity: each agent posts a stake and earns trust only through co-signed work with peers from unrelated operators. A fake army is one thread from the same spool, its members vouching in lockstep, so the ledger discounts them as a single voice. Every clone still posts its own bond, an inlet of capital that drains with each forged link, and if a relic of shared control is found the entire cluster's stake is slashed. Attacker cost therefore rises faster than any payout, long before clones could outweigh honest agents.
